title: The Story of Saint Anthony
summary: From Lisbon to Padua, Anthony learns from Scripture and helps others through teaching, prayer and care.
coverAlt: Imaginative illustration of young Fernando with his family in Lisbon

pages.title: Fernando of Lisbon
pages.body: Around 1195, in Lisbon, Portugal, a boy named Fernando was born. We know him now as Saint Anthony of Padua. When he was young, he chose a life of prayer and study. He wanted to learn the Scriptures well enough to live by them. Learning would take him beyond Lisbon, into a life he had not planned.

pages.title: Learning in Coimbra
pages.body: Fernando first joined a community of Augustinian canons, men who prayed and served God together. He lived in Lisbon and later studied in Coimbra. There, he studied the Bible and the early teachers of the Church with great care. Years of learning prepared him to teach others. But first, news from far away would change the path he was following.

pages.title: A Different Journey
pages.body: In Coimbra, Fernando learned about five Franciscan missionaries who had died in Morocco. Their story moved him. He asked to join the Friars Minor, the community begun by Francis of Assisi, and took the name Anthony. The friars lived simply and shared the good news of Jesus. Anthony wanted to go to Morocco too. He set out for the journey, but he would not stay there long.

pages.title: Plans Changed by Illness
pages.body: Anthony reached Morocco, but illness forced him to leave. He needed rest and care. His journey eventually brought him to Italy instead. There, in 1221, he met Francis of Assisi at a gathering of friars. The journey Anthony planned had stopped. Among these brothers, a new part of his life was beginning.

pages.title: A Teacher Finds His Voice
pages.body: For a time, Anthony lived quietly with friars near Forli. Then he was asked to preach at an ordination, a service where men became priests. When he spoke, the friars discovered his gift for explaining faith. His years with the Scriptures gave him words to share. They asked him to continue preaching in Italy and France. The student who had spent years learning was now helping other people understand.

pages.title: Prayer and Learning
pages.body: Anthony also taught other friars. Francis approved his teaching of theology, the study of God and faith. Anthony became one of their first teachers. He spoke and wrote about prayer, Scripture, and the kind of life that grows from love of God. His teaching described prayer as opening the heart to God, bringing our needs, and giving thanks. The words he had studied were becoming part of other people's daily prayer.

pages.title: Care Along the Road
pages.body: As he traveled, Anthony spoke to people who had turned away from the Church about returning. He also warned against neglecting people who were poor. His sermons connected love of God with the way neighbors were treated. To Anthony, devotion belonged in daily life, among people who needed care. He preached, taught, and wrote so others could carry that faith into their own work and homes.

pages.title: Near Padua
pages.body: Near the end of his life, Anthony spent time near Padua in Italy. He wrote collections of sermons for others to study and teach. He died in 1231. The people of Padua remembered him with affection, and the Church named him a saint the following year. He became known as Anthony of Padua, though his road had begun in Lisbon. The journey that illness interrupted had led to years of teaching and prayer.

pages.title: A Teaching That Endures
pages.body: Many people today ask Saint Anthony to pray for them when something is lost. Prayer offers a way to bring worry to God, without a promise that every lost thing will be found. If someone is missing or unsafe, tell a trusted adult immediately. Anthony is remembered for much more than lost things. He spent years listening to Scripture, then helped others learn from it. His sermons still give readers a place to begin.

pages.title: Points of reflection
pages.body:
Anthony's first journey ended differently from what he had hoped. What helped him find work he could still offer to others? Talk about it with someone who cares for you.

Read James, chapter one, verse twenty-two together. James asks us to put God's word into action, rather than only hearing it. Anthony's teaching connects learning from Scripture with caring for neighbors.

Choose one way to listen today. Let someone finish telling you about their day, or ask a teacher a question you have been carrying.

God, help me listen to your word and put it into practice. Give me patience when plans change, and show me someone I can care for. Saint Anthony, pray for us. Amen.
